source_candidate.claim_family: FLEX long-horizon task routing: train/eval task-identity assumptions and fail-open routing boundary

primary_sources.title: Beyond Routing Saturation: A Long-Horizon Class-Incremental Perspective on Expert Routing in Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

mechanical_findings.finding: FLEX is explicitly a 34-task ordered benchmark in code. Each task carries cur_task, source_task_name/source_task_id, output_dir and previous_task metadata, so task boundaries and exact task identity are available to the training/orchestration layer.
mechanical_findings.scope: Benchmark/config contract; this does not by itself imply oracle inference.

mechanical_findings.finding: PureLoRA training uses the CLContext task_id (or configured cur_task) to activate exactly that expert and to accumulate routing features into that exact task-indexed prototype/router class. The PROOF-style router likewise receives task_id and trains current-task features against target=task_id. Therefore routed methods are supervised task-as-class learners at training time, not unsupervised discovery of latent task identity.

The ordinary PureLoRA configuration sets oracle_expert_routing=false. In non-oracle evaluation, on_input_prep computes routing weights from image/text features and uses eval_task_id only for routing-match accounting when usable routing features/logits exist.
mechanical_findings.scope: This supports genuine feature-based unknown-task routing in the normal successful-feature path.

mechanical_findings.finding: However, the evaluation engine supplies eval_task_id to model loading and prepare_next_task; prepare_next_task sets model.current_task_id and invokes integration.prepare_for_new_task(eval_task_id). PureLoRA prepare_for_new_task sets self.cur_task to that ground-truth eval task and initializes a one-hot mixture for it.
mechanical_findings.scope: Pinned shared evaluation engine plus PureLoRA integration.

mechanical_findings.finding: Several non-oracle router failure/empty-feature paths fall back to self.cur_task. Because evaluation has just set self.cur_task from the ground-truth eval_task_id, a missing routing tower/feature, empty classifier logits, unavailable prototype, or analogous fallback can become a ground-truth-task one-hot route even though oracle_expert_routing=false.
mechanical_findings.scope: Source-reachable fail-open path. No claim is made here about how often it occurred in the paper's reported FLEX runs.

verdict.summary: The public FLEX routing stack is not simply oracle-routed: its normal non-oracle path predicts task/expert from image/text features, and oracle_expert_routing defaults false. But the evaluator still knows the ground-truth eval task and synchronizes it into current task state. Because non-oracle routing fallbacks use that current task, the public implementation has a source-reachable fail-open path in which routing failure reverts to the ground-truth expert. FLEX should therefore be described as supervised task-as-class routing with feature-based inference under successful routing-feature availability, not as a task-identity-sealed evaluator under all failure modes.
scope_corrections: Do not call FLEX routing unsupervised task discovery: exact task labels/boundaries supervise router state during training.
Do not call the normal successful-feature path oracle routing: oracle_expert_routing is false by default and feature-derived weights are used when available.
Do not claim the reported paper gains are caused by the fail-open fallback without measuring fallback incidence in the exact released experiment logs.

For a strict unknown-task evaluation contract, ground-truth eval_task_id should be kept out of mutable routing state and used only after prediction for scoring; missing-feature/empty-logit cases should fail closed or use a task-agnostic fallback.
